features.title: Edit/Run Manual Board Prototype
features.description: Build the smallest usable Edit/Run split on top of scenario load/save. Edit mode edits the scenario definition only and exposes four editable state panels: Board State for scenario-wide/global state such as trackers, decks, event piles, setup variables, and metadata; Object State for any Entity/Object such as character pawns, troop stacks, cards, tokens, dice, and their sheet/counter state; Location State for each Location's semantic state such as name, region/area membership, recruitment availability, terrain/tile bindings, haven/stronghold flags, slots, and notes; and Edge State for graph connection semantics such as directed/undirected movement, traversal cost, labels, locks, and notes. Edit mode also manages asset manifest, Board Template, background, Locations, Edges, board zones, default placement slots, and Setup Preset entities/cards/tokens/counters. Edit mode does not create or mutate runtime scenario state. Run mode opens a finalized scenario, freezes the Board Template and Setup Preset, derives the initial runtime snapshot from that setup, and supports semantic manual board operations: move Location-bound Entities between Locations, adjust stacked troop/token/dice counters, move cards between deck/discard/hand/display zones, inspect current state, save the runtime snapshot, and reload it. This feature intentionally ignores automatic setup parsing, event triggers, path validation, Cut-in rendering, online services, and game-specific rules.

features.title: Manual Card Decks, Piles, and Zones
features.description: Close the biggest manual setup gap by adding a generic card-zone model before movement validation. CARD assets and card-slice collections must be representable as ordered card refs inside named zones such as deck, discard, hand, display, objective area, unused box, and temporary setup piles. The model must support manual setup operations for create zone, order cards, shuffle with deterministic test injection or explicit saved order, draw/deal/move cards between zones, flip face up/down, inspect a pile, and serialize through .lorecanvas packages. It must stay generic: no hard-coded LOTR deck names, card effects, or automatic rule resolution. LOTRRule.pdf setup coverage should drive validation: special shadow cards start in shadow discard, the remaining shadow cards form the shadow deck, objective cards are faceup in an objective display, Skies Darken cards can be set aside, event cards can be selected by player count, event and region cards can form the player deck, starting hands can be dealt, and unused cards can be kept out of play.

features.title: Manual Dice Pools and Roll State
features.description: Add generic dice setup and manual roll state for board games that use custom dice. TOKEN assets with die metadata must define named dice, ordered face refs, and reusable dice pools. Run mode must support manual or deterministic-test rolling, preserving last result, roll history, and selected face overrides without resolving game-specific effects. Serialization must preserve dice definitions and current roll state. LOTR fixture validation should use local-fixtures/lotr/LotR-FotF/dice-face-plan.json to represent combat and search dice faces, then prove a scenario can record search and battle rolls generically without implementing LOTR search or battle rules.

features.title: Manual Tile and Marker Slots
features.description: Make TILE and marker setup explicit instead of relying only on freeform placed images. Add generic slot state for board Locations, tracks, and display zones so a tile or marker can be bound to a named slot, replaced, cleared, or moved while keeping a visual placement in sync. This must cover terrain/condition overlays, haven or stronghold replacements, track markers, and display slots without adding game-specific semantics. LOTRRule.pdf setup coverage should prove threat and hope markers can start on dotted track slots, the Eye marker can start in Eriador, haven/stronghold tile assets can remain available for later replacement, and objective/card display areas can own named slots.
features.verification: npx vitest run tests/engine/slot.test.ts tests/state/boardStore.test.ts tests/engine/serialization.test.ts; browser verification for assigning, replacing, clearing, and saving Location/track/display slots

features.title: Manual Pawn Stacks and Supply Pools
features.description: Promote count-bearing PAWN/TOKEN objects from loose JSON fields into a generic manual stack workflow. Edit mode must create setup stacks at Locations or supply zones, set count and capacity, split/merge stacks, and bind visual placements to Location state. Run mode must move or adjust stacks without mutating the frozen setup. The feature must remain category/state driven and not encode LOTR troop rules. LOTRRule.pdf setup coverage should validate fixed friendly troop stacks, remaining friendly supply by army, fixed shadow troop stacks, remaining shadow supply, Nazgul stacks, Eye/marker objects, and character pawn starting placements from character cards.
features.verification: npx vitest run tests/engine/stack.test.ts tests/state/pawnStackStore.test.ts tests/engine/serialization.test.ts; browser verification for create/split/merge/move stack, supply adjustment, save, load, and run-mode restore

features.title: LOTR FotF Manual Setup Validation
features.description: Use the ignored local fixture local-fixtures/lotr/LotR-FotF to validate that the generic manual setup surface can express the setup section of LOTRRule.pdf end to end. The test must import the manifest, create the board, Locations, Edges, card zones/decks, dice definitions, tile/marker slots, pawn stacks, supply pools, objective display, player hands, set-aside/unused cards, and unresolved random setup instructions where human choice or randomness is required. It must then enter Run mode, freeze setup, round-trip through save/load, and prove no product code contains LOTR-specific branches. This is setup validation only; it must not implement movement validation, automatic shadow-card resolution, battle/search rules, tracker automation, rule triggers, or Cut-in rendering.

features.title: Graph Movement Validation
features.description: Implement generic graph movement validation only after the manual setup component surface is validated. Expose an engine API that determines whether a path-capable Entity can move from its current Location to a target Location using existing Edges. The first version is adjacency/connectivity only and must not introduce grid, distance, A*, or game-specific movement assumptions.

features.title: Manual Global Tracker State
features.description: Add generic Global Trackers as manually editable scenario state after setup validation. Trackers represent values such as Threat, Time, Sanity, Doom, Hope, or any scenario-defined counter, and must serialize through .lorecanvas packages. This feature should not yet drive automatic visual filters or rule triggers.

features.title: Deferred JSON Rule Trigger Engine
features.description: After the manual setup surface, movement validation, and tracker state are stable, implement the generic event listener and JSON rule tree engine. It should accept triggers such as ENTITY_MOVE, ENTITY_STATE_CHANGE, TRACKER_CHANGE, CARD_ZONE_CHANGE, DICE_ROLL, STACK_CHANGE, and MANUAL_TRIGGER, evaluate conditions, and emit actions without hard-coding LOTR or any other specific game.

features.title: Deferred Cut-in Renderer
features.description: Implement the CCFOLIA-style theatrical rendering lane after the rule engine exists. Cut-in payloads should support overlays, image references, slide-in presentation, typewriter text, and rule hint panels. The renderer consumes commands only and must not decide game rules.

mvpFocus.summary: The Edit/Run board MVP and Maker map editor are stable enough for graph editing, image import, asset placement, and selected-object inspection. The next gap is full manual setup for complex American/story board games: card decks and zones, custom dice, tile/marker slots, pawn stacks, and supply pools must be first-class enough to reproduce LOTRRule.pdf setup before movement validation or automation work resumes.

modeModel.editMode: Edits setup definition only through four state surfaces plus structural assets: Board State for global scenario state, Object State for Entity/Object state, Location State for per-Location semantic state, and Edge State for per-connection semantic state. It also edits asset manifest, Board Template, background, Locations, Edges, zones, default placement slots, and Setup Preset entities/cards/tokens/counters. It does not create runtime scenario state.
modeModel.runMode: Consumes a finalized scenario definition, freezes Board Template and Setup Preset, derives an initial runtime snapshot, then allows manual runtime operations such as moving Location-bound Entities, adjusting stacks/counters, moving cards between zones, and saving/reloading current runtime state.

lotrSetupRequirements: Board is placed as the central background; threat and hope markers start on dotted track spaces.
Two special shadow cards begin in shadow discard; remaining shadow cards form the shadow deck.
Friendly troop stacks start at named colored Locations with remaining supply by army.
Shadow troop stacks start at named red Locations, with 9 random shadow-card deployments recorded as unresolved setup randomness and remaining shadow supply preserved.
Nazgul stacks and Eye marker start in specified regions.
Objective display includes Destroy the One Ring plus other selected objectives; objective setup instructions may require character-card selection.
Each player receives two character cards, reference cards, character figure placements, and a starting hand from the player deck.
Skies Darken cards are set aside; event cards are selected by player count; selected events and region cards form the player deck; unused event/Skies cards leave play.
Solo setup adds Frodo and Sam, four other faceup character cards, a solo token on the leftmost character, and starting figure placements.
